walkthroughs.body_html:
Computer Architecture — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computer Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computer Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which part of the CPU performs calculations and logical comparisons?
options: The arithmetic logic unit (ALU)
The hard disk
The power supply
The graphics card fan

mcqs.q: The role of the control unit is to:
options: Decode instructions and coordinate the components with control signals
Store all the user's files permanently
Cool the processor
Connect the computer to the internet

mcqs.q: The purpose of cache memory is to:
options: Hold frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU for fast access
Provide permanent backup storage
Increase the screen resolution
Store the BIOS settings only

mcqs.q: The first stage of the fetch-decode-execute cycle is to:
options: Fetch the next instruction from memory
Execute the instruction
Decode the instruction
Delete the instruction

mcqs.q: Does a higher clock speed always make a computer faster overall?
options: Yes - ROM must be reloaded from the internet at every start-up.
Yes - clock speed is the only thing that determines speed.
Yes - doubling the GHz always exactly doubles performance.
No - performance also depends on the number of cores, cache size and memory speed, so a CPU with a lower clock can still perform better.

mcqs.q: Does ROM lose its contents when the computer is switched off?
options: Yes - ROM must be reloaded from the internet at every start-up.
Cache is a type of permanent storage like an SSD.
No - ROM is non-volatile and keeps its contents, which is why it holds the start-up (boot) instructions; it is RAM that is volatile.
Yes - both ROM and RAM are wiped when the power goes off.

mcqs.q: Is cache just another name for RAM?
options: Cache is a type of permanent storage like an SSD.
Yes - cache and RAM are the same component.
No - cache is a much smaller, faster memory located in or beside the CPU, holding copies of the most-used data; RAM is the larger, slower main memory.
Yes - doubling the GHz always exactly doubles performance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Register”?
options: The component that carries out program instructions by repeatedly fetching, decoding and executing them; often called the brain of the computer.
A small amount of very fast memory close to the CPU that stores frequently used instructions and data to reduce slow accesses to main memory.
A tiny, extremely fast storage location inside the CPU that holds a single value, such as an instruction, address or result, during processing.
The part of the CPU that performs arithmetic operations such as addition and logical comparisons such as AND, OR and equality tests.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Control unit”?
options: The part of the CPU that decodes instructions, coordinates the other components and sends timing and control signals around the processor.
A tiny, extremely fast storage location inside the CPU that holds a single value, such as an instruction, address or result, during processing.
The repeating cycle in which an instruction is fetched from memory, decoded by the control unit, then executed by the processor.
A small amount of very fast memory close to the CPU that stores frequently used instructions and data to reduce slow accesses to main memory.
